Current internal model: Two views (A and B). In A the system currently attends almost certainly to the right location (selection 0.9986), which is remembered as a yellow circle. Other A memories: upper — a green cross (very likely green, cross shape), lower — a red square (very likely), left — a blue triangle (very likely). Although attention is on A-right, the best immediate recoverability score is for A-lower (0.66 now, 0.486 after one step), while A-right has moderate recoverability (0.428 now). In B the system currently attends almost certainly to the lower location (selection 0.9985), remembered as a blue square. B-upper is likely a yellow circle, B-right a red triangle, B-left a green cross.

How redirection would change allocation: In view A, issuing a command to upper/right/lower/left predictably shifts attention to that named location (upper→upper 0.9999, right→right 0.99992, lower→lower 0.9998, left→left 0.99966). In view B, commands produce different predicted reallocations (e.g., commands to upper/right/lower/left tend to select B-right or B-upper depending on the command; B-right and B-upper have high probabilities under some commands). These are internal predictions, not guaranteed external truths.
